# Homework overview

You will continue with the [Great Lakes commercial fish catch records](http://www.glfc.org/great-lakes-databases.php) and the [Great Lakes Fish Stocking database](http://www.glfc.org/fishstocking/index.htm), both maintained by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

The goal of the assignment is a merged table in which **each row is one year of Lake Michigan Chinook Salmon catch and stocking**, with both weights in the same units (thousands of pounds).

## Learning goals

By the end of this homework, you should be able to:  

  * Select, filter, and summarize two related tables until they share a join key.
  * Convert units and rename columns so a join is valid.
  * Explain what `left_join()`, `right_join()`, `inner_join()`, `full_join()`, and `anti_join()` keep.
  * Reshape joined columns with `pivot_longer()` and plot the long table.

## Deliverable

Complete **`hw-03-starter.Rmd`**. Your finished starter file should contain your code, plots, and written responses and should Knit successfully from top to bottom.

## Reproducibility rule

Your analysis must work from top to bottom. Knit frequently.

## Exercise 3 — Filter to Chinook Salmon in Lake Michigan

**Goal:** Keep U.S. Chinook Salmon records for Lake Michigan.

Chinook Salmon is `"Chinook Salmon"` in `catch_data` and `"CHS"` in `fish_stock`. Lake Michigan is `"Michigan"` in `catch_data` and `"MI"` in `fish_stock`. Restrict stocking events to the U.S. states that border Lake Michigan: Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois, and Indiana.

```{r filter-catch-demo, echo = TRUE, eval = F}
catch_data <- catch_data %>% 
  filter(region == "U.S. Total",
         species == "___",
         lake == "___")
```

```{r filter-stock-demo, echo = TRUE, eval = F}
fish_stock <- fish_stock %>% 
  filter(___ %in% c("MI", "WI", "IL", "IN"),
         SPECIES == "___",
         LAKE == "MI")
```

## Harmonize names and units

The tables still disagree in two ways:

- `catch_data` uses lowercase names, and `values` is already in **thousands of pounds**.
- `fish_stock_yearly` uses uppercase names, and `STOCK_WEIGHT_YR` is in **kilograms**.

Run the two provided chunks in your starter file (set `eval` to `TRUE`). They rename the year column, convert kilograms to thousands of pounds, and rename catch `values`.

```{marginfigure}
1 kg ≈ 2.205 lb, so thousands of pounds = kg × 2.205 / 1000. 
```

```{r finalize-fish-stock-demo, echo = TRUE}
fish_stock_yearly <- fish_stock_yearly %>% 
  rename(year = YEAR) %>% 
  mutate(stock_weight_yr_lbs = as.integer(STOCK_WEIGHT_YR * 2.205 / 1000)) %>% 
  select(year, stock_weight_yr_lbs)
```

```{r finalize-catch-data-demo, echo = TRUE}
catch_data <- catch_data %>% 
  rename(catch_weight_yr_lbs = values)
```

Confirm that both tables now have a `year` column and a weight column in thousands of pounds.

## Exercise 6 — Six joins

**Goal:** Join the two year-level tables six ways and explain what each join keeps.

Join `catch_data` and `fish_stock_yearly` with `left_join()`, `right_join()`, `inner_join()`, `full_join()`, and `anti_join()` in both directions. Look at each result. For every join, write 1–2 sentences: which rows were kept, and what R does when a year exists on only one side.

The two `anti_join()` chunks are filled in for you; write narrative for those as well.

```{r anti-join-v1-demo, echo = TRUE}
catch_data %>% 
  anti_join(fish_stock_yearly)
```

```{r anti-join-v2-demo, echo = TRUE}
fish_stock_yearly %>% 
  anti_join(catch_data)
```

# Data dictionary

### fishing.csv (`catch_data`)

| variable    | class     | description                                                         |
|:------------|:----------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| year        | double    | Year of the estimate                                                |
| lake        | character | Lake name                                                           |
| species     | character | Species of fish                                                     |
| grand_total | double    | Grand total reported for that lake-species-year                     |
| comments    | character | Notes from the data providers                                       |
| region      | character | U.S. or Canadian reporting region (coding is inconsistent)          |
| values      | double    | Harvest rounded to the nearest thousand pounds                      |

### great-lakes-fish-stock.csv (`fish_stock`)

| variable    | class     | description                                            |
|:------------|:----------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| YEAR        | double    | Year of stocking, YYYY                                 |
| MONTH       | double    | Month of stocking (not always reported)                |
| LAKE        | character | Great Lake, abbreviated                                |
| STATE_PROV  | character | State or province, abbreviated                         |
| SPECIES     | character | Species code                                           |
| NO_STOCKED  | double    | Number of fish stocked                                 |
| AGEMONTH    | double    | Age in months (not always reported)                    |
| WEIGHT      | double    | Total weight of fish stocked, in kilograms             |
